title: Frontend e2e fixture provider — non-blocking review follow-up
description: Non-blocking finding from pr-reviewer's review of PR #104 (frontend-e2e-tests-followups), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so it isn't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: backend/app/data/fixture_provider.py's get_weekly_ohlcv (line 88) was changed in PR #104 to call self.get_daily_ohlcv(ticker) instead of self._series(ticker), per PR #103's follow-up finding asking it to 'resample get_daily_ohlcv's own output instead of independently recomputing the series'. Verified this produces byte-identical output (confirmed with FixtureDataProvider().get_weekly_ohlcv('AAPL') vs a manual daily.resample('W-FRI') on get_daily_ohlcv's own output -- .equals() is True), so it's not a correctness issue. But it does NOT actually achieve the stated performance goal: get_daily_ohlcv itself has no memoization/caching (it's `return self._series(ticker)`, recomputed fresh on every call), so self.get_daily_ohlcv(ticker) inside get_weekly_ohlcv still re-runs the full ~420-iteration RNG loop from scratch every time, exactly as self._series(ticker) did before. The motivating scenario the original PR #103 follow-up finding cited -- a request needing both daily and weekly data for the same ticker (app/api/routers/stocks.py's GET .../analysis and GET .../history handlers, and app/api/routers/watchlist.py, all call both provider.get_daily_ohlcv(ticker) and provider.get_weekly_ohlcv(ticker) separately on the same provider instance) -- still runs the RNG loop twice, unchanged by this fix, since there's no shared/cached frame between the two separate calls. The fix only changed the internal call from self._series(ticker) to self.get_daily_ohlcv(ticker), which is functionally identical in cost (confirmed by timing: 200x get_daily_ohlcv ~1.2s vs 200x get_weekly_ohlcv ~1.83s, consistent with get_weekly_ohlcv running the loop once per call, same as before -- no doubling was ever happening *within* a single get_weekly_ohlcv call, so this change didn't remove one). If this fixture-only, e2e-suite-only performance genuinely needs addressing, get_daily_ohlcv/_series would need real memoization (e.g. functools.lru_cache keyed by ticker, or an instance-level dict) so a get_weekly_ohlcv call can reuse a get_daily_ohlcv call already made earlier in the same request -- not just call through the public method, which still recomputes from scratch. Given this only affects the no-network e2e fixture (never the live app, never the pytest suite), the cost is low (sub-millisecond per extra call) -- low priority, but the fix as landed doesn't do what its own commit message and the task checklist entry it closed claim it does.

decisions.decision: Added memoization to FixtureDataProvider.get_daily_ohlcv as a per-instance dict cache (self._daily_cache, keyed by upper-cased ticker) rather than functools.lru_cache on the method, and left get_weekly_ohlcv unchanged (it already calls self.get_daily_ohlcv per PR #104, so it now benefits from the cache for free).
decisions.rationale: app.api.dependencies.get_data_provider constructs a fresh FixtureDataProvider() per request, so a plain instance attribute already scopes the cache exactly right: shared across get_daily_ohlcv/get_weekly_ohlcv calls within one request, and discarded with the instance at the end of it. functools.lru_cache decorating an instance method keys each cache entry on (self, ticker) but the cache dict itself lives on the *function* (i.e. the class), not the instance -- it would keep a strong reference to every FixtureDataProvider instance ever constructed for as long as the process runs (only ever an issue for a long-lived process serving many e2e requests, but a real one), and would need an explicit maxsize/eviction policy to bound that. No cache-invalidation/TTL logic is needed either way: get_daily_ohlcv's output is a pure, deterministic function of ticker alone (seeded RNG keyed off the ticker name, per the class docstring), so a cached value never goes stale -- verified safe against aliasing too, since no caller in app/api/routers/{stocks,watchlist,portfolio}.py or app/signals/*.py mutates a provider-returned OHLCV frame in place (grepped for inplace=True / column-assignment on a provider frame; found none), and _trim_to_range's 'max' branch already returns the exact same object reference as the live providers do today, so sharing one cached object across both calls doesn't introduce a new aliasing risk beyond what already existed.

review.notes: Full review: backend suite (source .venv/bin/activate && pytest --cov=app --cov-report=term-missing --cov-fail-under=90) 578 passed, 99.87% total coverage, 100% on the changed file (backend/app/data/fixture_provider.py). ruff check app/ and mypy both clean. code-review skill (medium effort) found zero findings. Frontend untouched by this PR (git diff --stat main...HEAD -- frontend/ is empty); last known state clean per PR #133. Not backend/signals or backend/portfolio and skill isn't verify-elder-signal, so that check doesn't apply; no new module/dependency/layer added, so architecture-review doesn't apply; no frontend component touched, so the placement check doesn't apply; no API route/schema touched, so no openapi.json regeneration is required (confirmed via git diff --stat against backend/app/api/ and backend/openapi.json, both empty). UI-facing: this change only affects app/data/fixture_provider.py, which backs the endpoints the frontend consumes, so I ran both the persisted e2e suite (make e2e -- all 16 Playwright specs across dashboard/navigation/portfolio/stock-analysis/watchlist passed, including the unknown-ticker 404 edge case and range/interval toggles) and attempted an interactive Playwright-MCP walkthrough; no browser MCP tool was available in this session's toolset, so that specific interactive step could not be performed -- the persisted e2e run (which drives the exact same fixture-backed stack through a real Chromium browser, golden path plus edge cases, and asserts no console errors on load) is the closest available substitute and found no issues. Mutation-safety scrutiny (the specific ask for this review): grepped the whole backend for `inplace=True` and `.loc[...] =` assignment on any DataFrame -- zero hits anywhere in app/. Traced every caller of get_daily_ohlcv/get_weekly_ohlcv (app/api/routers/{stocks,watchlist,portfolio}.py, app/portfolio/pricing.py, app/signals/engine.py, app/portfolio/risk.py, app/signals/{impulse,triple_screen}.py) -- every one of them only reads columns, slices (.iloc/.tail/dropna, all non-mutating, return-new-frame operations), or passes the frame through as an argument; none reassigns into the frame's existing columns/rows. app/api/routers/stocks.py's _trim_to_range already returned the exact same object reference on the 'max'/empty-frame branch before this PR (pre-existing behavior, not new aliasing risk), consistent with the PR's own claim. TestMemoization in backend/tests/unit/data/test_fixture_provider.py correctly asserts object identity (`first is second`), call-count via `mocker.spy(FixtureDataProvider, "_series")` + `assert_called_once()` (covering both same-ticker-twice and get_weekly_ohlcv-reusing-get_daily_ohlcv's cache), case-insensitive keying, and per-instance (not global) cache scope with a value-equality check across instances -- these are real identity/count assertions, not shallow value-only checks. No blocking findings. No non-blocking findings either (code-review agent's independent pass also returned zero findings), so no follow-up task was filed.
